efficient presentation of measles virus antigens by MHC class II molecules is dependent on CD46, and is an endocytic process.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

CD46‐dependent presentation of measles virus antigens to CD4+ T cells is a complex process which involves the capture of MV particles by their receptor, their endocytosis, their disruption and processing of viral proteins in endosome/lysosomes and their loading into MHC II molecules.
the CD46 receptor of MV plays a key role in the uptake and presentation to T cells of MV‐H and MV‐N, and that the endocytosis of MV‐N is more efficient than that of MV‐H.
the efficient MHC class II‐restricted presentation by B cells of MV to T cells relies upon its capture via its receptor CD46, which targets the virus to an endosomal pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD46‐mediation is an efficient way for MV to reach its cellular target cells and for its proteins to be presented by MHC class II molecules.
efficient presentation of MV‐N to CD4+ T cells relies on an endosomal pathway involving CD46‐mediatied internalization of the virus.
CD46 is a major factor in the efficient presentation of MV‐derived epitopes by B cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CD46 receptor is a critical factor in the efficient uptake and antigen processing of measles virus by human B lymphocytes.
CD46 is a major player in the efficient uptake and presentation of MV to T cells.
CD46 can be used as a receptor to target antigens to the endocytic compartment for presentation by MHC class II.
